evidence.title: Warp Terminal
evidence.locator: Build, review and ship; OS downloads
evidence.finding: Warp Terminal advertises Mac, Windows and Linux clients, agent sessions in vertical tabs and an integrated review/editing flow.

evidence.title: Warp Terminal documentation bundle
evidence.locator: Sessions; SSH; Tabs behavior; Block sharing; Warp Drive
evidence.finding: The first-party documentation bundle describes SSH workflows, restored layouts, tab error indicators and reusable shared materials.

evidence.title: Warp pricing
evidence.locator: Warp Terminal and agents plans, checked 7 November 2026
evidence.finding: Free, Build, Max, Business and custom Enterprise plans distinguish included usage, collaboration and customer-supplied inference.

evidence.title: Platform usage
evidence.locator: How platform usage is measured; when charges apply
evidence.finding: Cloud runs incur platform usage even on self-hosted workers. Eligible dollar-billed plans charge $3 per agent-hour; inference and hosted compute are separate.

evidence.title: Warp Agent CLI
evidence.finding: Standalone warp command runs the native agent in any terminal including SSH, with saved account conversations, shell, diffs, approvals, context and model selection.

evidence.title: Warp Agent CLI quickstart
evidence.finding: CLI supports macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, Linux x64/Arm64 and Windows x64/Arm64. Browser device code or WARP_API_KEY authentication is documented.

evidence.title: Third-party CLI agents overview
evidence.finding: Warp detects third-party coding agents in terminal panes with rich input, per-agent status, code review and remote control. They are separate from the native conversation and agent-management panels.

evidence.title: Set up Claude Code
evidence.finding: Warp documents running Claude Code with a paid Claude account or API credits and authenticating with its own provider login.

evidence.title: Agent Session Sharing
evidence.finding: Local Warp and third-party sessions can be shared to signed-in web/mobile viewers. Editors can prompt and execute commands concurrently; data expires after roughly one week and secret redaction is not applied.

evidence.title: Agent planning and execution
evidence.finding: Plans are editable, versioned, selectively executable and saved in Warp Drive with Markdown export and reuse across conversations.

evidence.title: Agent Task Lists
evidence.finding: The agent creates sequential task lists automatically for complex requests and shows pending, active, completed and cancelled statuses inside conversations.

evidence.title: Rules for agents
evidence.finding: Global and repository AGENTS.md/WARP.md rules have documented precedence and create/edit/delete controls. WARP.md wins when both exist in one directory.

evidence.title: Model Context Protocol
evidence.finding: Warp local agents support command, Streamable HTTP and SSE MCP servers, credentials via env/headers, and local configuration; launched servers stop when Warp exits.

evidence.title: Codebase Context
evidence.finding: Git-tracked repositories and worktrees index separately; code is not stored on Warp servers. Sync is periodic, at new conversations or manual; indexing delay can expose stale context.

evidence.title: Git worktrees
evidence.finding: Warp supports separate Git worktrees with independent diffs, indexing and branch status for parallel local agent work.

evidence.title: Running orchestrated agents
evidence.finding: A Warp app parent proposes a child-agent breakdown through /orchestrate or /plan. Approved children can run locally or in cloud environments, with status pills and retained child conversations.

evidence.title: Profiles & Permissions
evidence.finding: Profiles configure models and per-tool autonomy, command allow/denylists and MCP tool access. Run-until-completion can bypass denylist prompts for a task.

evidence.title: Roles and permissions
evidence.finding: Owner, Admin and Member have explicit administration and usage boundaries; organization-enforced settings cannot be overridden.

evidence.title: Privacy and data control
evidence.finding: Paid plans may disable Help improve Warp and crash reports while retaining AI. Free AI requires telemetry. Vendor documentation labels client source AGPLv3, but its linked source license was not retrievable in this pass.

evidence.title: Architecture and deployment
evidence.finding: Warp separates client/execution from its hosted orchestration, observability and inference control plane; customer-hosted workers still send prompts/transcripts through Warp servers.

evidence.title: Warp Trust Center
evidence.finding: Vendor states SOC2 TypeII covering security, availability, confidentiality and processing integrity; Enterprise reports are request-only. No audit issuer/period was exposed.

evidence.title: Interactive Code Review
evidence.finding: Inline comments on Git-indexed diffs can be batched and sent to native or supported third-party agents for revisions.

evidence.title: Agent conversations in Warp Agent CLI
evidence.finding: Conversations save automatically, sync across account clients and resume after exiting. Markdown export and Ctrl+C cancellation are documented; restoring a process is separate.

evidence.title: warpdotdev/warp LICENSE-AGPL
evidence.finding: The client repository linked from the privacy page contains the GNU Affero General Public License v3 text; GitHub reports the repository license as AGPL-3.0.

evidence.title: warpdotdev/warp README
evidence.locator: README.md at abb3fe33e004f7b1de540fecd6e3eec20dbc1883, Licensing and Open Source & Contributing
evidence.finding: The warpui_core and warpui UI framework crates are MIT; the rest of the client repository is AGPL v3. The README says Warp's client codebase is open source in this repository.

evidence.title: Warp Agents overview
evidence.locator: What makes the Warp Agent different section, 'Many agents at once' bullet
evidence.finding: The Warp Agent can run several conversations in parallel, tracked in the Agent Management Panel, or a parent agent can spawn and coordinate child agents through orchestration.

deletion.answer: Rules can be deleted through their documented controls or project file edits.

indexing.answer: Warp automatically detects Git repositories and indexes each worktree independently.

freshness.answer: Sync is periodic, at new conversations or manually triggered; branch changes and slow networks can leave stale context temporarily.

human_visibility.answer: A conversation task-list chip opens the current progress list.

persistent_requirements.answer: Plans persist as reusable documents in Warp Drive.

human_edits.answer: Humans can reorganize and refine plan steps manually.

agent_edits.answer: Agents can revise sections and create a new version.

revisions.answer: Plan version history permits comparison and restoration.

implementation_links.answer: Referenced file paths link plans to the workspace; a selected plan section can be executed.

later_retrieval.answer: @plans searches previously saved plans for future conversations.

roles.answer: A native parent agent spawns and coordinates child agents.

model_harness_effort.answer: The plan orchestration configuration exposes model, harness, environment, host and parallelism.

results_return.answer: The proposal names each child’s expected output; parent and child conversations remain inspectable.

activation.answer: /orchestrate or /plan opens a proposal that the human approves before fan-out.

authentication.answer: Cloud children inherit the local parent’s authentication and account billing.

live_progress.answer: A pill bar shows parent and child names with live status badges.

natural_language.answer: /orchestrate accepts a natural-language task and proposed child boundaries.

discoverability.answer: The /orchestrate and /plan slash-command entry points are documented.

local.answer: Warp documents running multiple local agents on worktrees in user directories.

branch.answer: Each worktree has its own checked-out branch and Git status.

worktree.answer: Warp detects Git worktrees and supports parallel local agents in separate worktree directories.

code_separation.answer: Per-worktree review and indexing distinguish local working files; shared Git metadata still exists.

discussion.answer: Shared participants can add follow-up agent queries in the same session.

presence.answer: Multiple participants see each other’s cursors and avatars.

coprompting.answer: Granted editors can send agent queries and execute commands in the same shared session.

permissions.answer: The sharer grants view or edit access, can invite individuals or a team and can stop sharing.

organization_roles.answer: Single-team workspaces have Owner, Admin and Member roles.

membership.answer: Owners/admins invite, remove and promote/demote team members.

unauthorized_access.answer: Members use agents and shared resources within enforced administrator settings.

revocation.answer: Administrators can remove members and demote admins; only the owner transfers ownership.

command.answer: Command permissions, allowlists and denylists control approval prompts.

tool.answer: Profiles separately control file reads, diffs, planning, commands and MCP access.

lifetime.answer: Run-until-completion changes autonomy for the current task.

allow.answer: Always allow and command allowlists enable unattended actions.

deny.answer: Never disables supported actions; denylist entries ordinarily force a prompt.

enforcement.answer: Run-until-completion can bypass the command denylist; denylist matching is not an unconditional execution prohibition.

comments.answer: Reviewers annotate specific changed lines/blocks, batch comments and submit them to the agent.

request_changes.answer: The agent receives batched feedback and returns an updated diff.

retained_context.answer: Comments are anchored to file/line context for the agent.

same_task.answer: A collaborator with edit access can continue prompting the same shared session.

session_history.answer: Shared context includes prompt, responses, tools, plans and terminal output.

permissions.answer: The owner decides who can view or interact; workspace policy can disable sharing.

context_loss.answer: Shared-session data expires after approximately one week; it is not permanent task ownership storage.

branches.answer: Git status and review reflect the branch in the current worktree.

worktrees.answer: Warp recognizes worktree checkouts with per-worktree review and indexing.

findings.answer: Line/block comments collect concrete requested changes.

artifacts.answer: Review operates on actual Git-indexed file diffs.

request_changes.answer: Batched comments request agent revisions and another diff review.

vendor_dependencies.answer: Agent orchestration and inference route through Warp’s backend even when execution is customer hosted.

export.answer: Plans export as Markdown for repository storage or sharing.

formats.answer: Markdown export is documented for plans.

code_data.answer: With telemetry disabled no console interactions are persisted on Warp servers, according to the privacy documentation.

credentials.answer: Secret redaction is not applied to Session Sharing; visible secrets remain visible to authorized viewers.

artifacts.answer: Session sharing uploads scrollback and live output to Warp servers.

retention.answer: Shared-session data expires approximately one week after sharing.

deletion.answer: Stop sharing ends live access, but no per-session immediate-delete control is available before expiry; account-deletion jobs run every twenty-four hours.
